target_customer: Car owners buying an aftermarket highway autopilot kit at launch, later GM and robotaxi riders
problem: Highway driving was tedious and unsafe, and in 2014 no one sold self-driving capability for cars people already owned.
business_model: Hardware kit sale at 10,000 dollars at launch, later in-house autonomous vehicle development and robotaxi service

founders.name: Kyle Vogt
education: MIT, computer science and electrical engineering

competitors.name: Google self-driving car project
competitors.what: Prototype fully driverless cars built on Lexus vehicles

competitors.name: Tesla Autopilot concept
competitors.what: Driver assist approach that press compared to Cruise RP-1

technical_complexity.rationale: Perception, planning and safety for driving on public roads is research grade, and the 2014 kit required reliable sensing, actuation of an Audi A4 and safety validation by a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Strong engineering lead at first, but automakers and Google had far more resources, and the retrofit kit depended on one car model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GM acquired Cruise in May 2016 for 581 million dollars at closing per its filings, after initial reports of about 1 billion, then funded it with over 10 billion dollars before shutting the robotaxi effort in December 2024.

market_need_then: Press in June 2014 treated highway autopilot as a real consumer wish and the 10,000 dollar kit was pitched against Google's plan to offer self-driving cars between 2017 and 2020.

identity.visual_style: Product vehicles such as the Origin shuttle unveiled in 2020
identity.voice_and_tone: Safety and mission focused corporate voice per company statements

branding.brand_signature: Driverless orange-sensored robotaxi fleet in San Francisco
branding.community_and_virality: Wide press coverage of the 2014 kit and later robotaxi rides; also heavy negative coverage after the October 2023 incident.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely known as a leading robotaxi brand at its peak with press and city presence, but the brand name was generic and the 2023 incident damaged trust.

pivots.from: Aftermarket highway autopilot kit RP-1 for Audi A4
pivots.to: Full self-driving in cities for ride hailing
pivots.why: Sources say the greater challenge and market lay in city driving, so the retrofit plan was dropped.

outcome_analysis: Cruise was a fast YC success: a tiny team launched a highway autopilot kit in 2014, raised small rounds, pivoted to city driving and sold to GM in 2016 for 581 million dollars at closing. Under GM it raised billions, but an October 2023 pedestrian incident led to suspended permits, and in December 2024 GM stopped funding robotaxis citing the time and resources to scale and a more competitive market, then cut about half the remaining staff.
notes: Status Acquired matches the 2016 GM deal; GM wound down robotaxi operations in December 2024, which is later than the exit. Price: GM disclosed 581M consideration at closing (291M cash plus about 290M stock); earlier press said over 1B and YC says 1B; Fool valued it near 688M. The seed amount of 4.3M is from one investor page and a database, and TechCrunch says 12.5M Series A brought total funding to 16.8M, so exact seed and round dates are unverified (dated by year only). A database lists different seed figures and is ignored. Pre-deal valuation of about 90M post money is from Business Insider and unverified. The company website getcruise.com returned HTTP 503 so was not read. Later GM investor rounds (SoftBank 2.25B, Honda 750M) were in the Cruise unit after acquisition and are not recorded as rounds.
